First-stage strength of a proxy

Source: R/psvar.R
proxy_fstat.Rd

Three F statistics for the relevance of the proxy for the target shock: F from regressing the reduced-form residual of target on the proxy, F_robust its heteroskedasticity-robust (HC1) version (needs sandwich, else NA), and F_hac, the Montiel Olea-Stock-Watson (2021) Wald statistic \(T\hat\Gamma_j^2/\hat W_{\Gamma_{jj}}\) using the delta-method HAC covariance that also accounts for the estimation of the VAR coefficients. F_hac is the relevant statistic for varm_proxy_robust().

Usage

proxy_fstat(fit, m, target = 1L, nwlags = NULL)

Arguments

fit

a varm() object.

m

proxy: numeric vector, or T x r matrix of r proxies, aligned with the data (the first p rows are dropped to match the residuals).

target

variable(s) (name or position) whose impact response is normalised to size; length r.

nwlags

Newey-West truncation lag for F_hac; default floor(4 * (T/100)^(2/9)).

Value

named numeric c(F = , F_robust = , F_hac = ). With several instruments (m a matrix, target of the same length) a matrix with one row per target; F/F_robust are then joint statistics over the instruments and F_hac is NA (the MOSW sets are single-instrument).

See also

varm_proxy_robust()
